architecture.title: How it works
architecture.description: Next.js renders the shell. CheerpX runs guest programs locally in your browser.

compatibility.title: No Linux kernel
compatibility.description: CheerpX provides syscall compatibility for 32-bit x86 userspace. Not Docker, systemd or a full hardware VM. Some syscalls and apps may not work.

storage.title: Local, not immortal
storage.description: Files stay in this browser profile, on this site. Clearing site data or browser storage eviction can delete them. Running processes do not survive a reload.

network.title: Networking is optional
network.description: The desktop starts without guest networking. Internet access requires your own Tailscale account, an exit node and a suitable tailnet policy. Runtime and the base disk are delivered by external CDNs.

landing.licenseNote: MIT covers the original PocketOSix code. CheerpX is proprietary; Alpine and its packages have separate licenses.

run.saveUnavailable: Unavailable: CheerpX 1.4.0 has no verified public durable-flush API.
run.diskWriteDetails: Only files, packages and settings committed to browser storage survive reload. Guest writes may finish before that asynchronous commit. Reloading or leaving can lose recent changes; RAM, running processes and unsaved app documents are not preserved. Storage belongs to this browser profile and origin. Do not keep your only copy of important files here.
run.networkDetails: Tailscale connects only when you choose to. Internet access needs your own account, an external exit node and a suitable tailnet policy. A Tailscale IP or detected exit node does not prove internet access; verify it inside the guest. The desktop starts without guest networking.

docs.intro: Get started with your Alpine desktop, learn the controls, and understand how files and networking work.

start.intro: No installation or account is needed to open the desktop. Your browser needs internet access to download CheerpX and the base image.

launch.title: Launch the desktop
launch.detail: Select Launch to open /run, then choose > boot to start Alpine. Wait for the desktop to appear. The first boot may take a while; the logs show real activity, not a percentage estimate.

focus.title: Click inside the desktop
focus.detail: Click the guest display so keyboard input goes to Xorg and i3. After using a browser menu or dialog, close it and click the display again.

terminal.title: Open your first app
terminal.detail: Click Apps on the guest bar, then Terminal, and wait for the shell prompt before typing. Alt + Enter is also configured to launch a terminal; some browser or OS shortcuts may interfere. Alt + d opens the rofi app launcher. A desktop without open windows is not a loading screen.

keyboard.intro: The base image uses Alt as the i3 modifier (Mod1), not Super. If you edit the i3 configuration in the guest, your own bindings apply.
keyboard.tableCaption: More shortcuts from the base image's i3 configuration

fullscreen.action: Toggle fullscreen for the i3 window, not the browser

resize.action: Enter resize mode; Enter or Escape to leave

keyboard.caveat: Your operating system or browser may intercept shortcuts, even in fullscreen. If nothing happens, first check that the guest display has focus.
keyboard.tty: The browser terminal connects to the guest's real tty1, separate from an i3 terminal window. At the login prompt, the factory username is user and the factory password is password, unless you changed them. These are public image defaults, not personal secrets. There is no automatic login; boot output does not mean a shell is ready.
keyboard.input: Pasting from the browser clipboard directly into the guest display and sending keys from a mobile soft-key panel are not currently supported. Copying text in the browser does not send it to the guest. A desktop keyboard is recommended.

storage.intro: Changes to the root disk are stored locally in IndexedDB as an overlay on the base Alpine image. This saves disk changes, not a snapshot of the running desktop.

saved.title: What stays
saved.detail: Files, installed packages and settings committed to browser storage remain after a page reload. Guest writes can finish before the asynchronous browser commit; an immediate reload may lose recent changes.

session.title: What restarts
session.detail: RAM, running processes, and terminal sessions do not survive reload. Unsaved work in an app is not a saved file.

location.title: Where files live
location.detail: Storage belongs to one browser profile and one origin (scheme, host, and port). Another profile, device, preview URL, or port has a separate disk. Clearing site data deletes the local changes.

quota.title: Storage limits
quota.detail: Browser quotas limit space, and the browser may evict data. Storage usage is an estimate for the whole origin, not the exact size of the guest disk.

storage.persist: The disk controls on /run can ask the browser to protect storage from automatic eviction. The browser may grant or deny the request. A grant does not prevent manual site-data deletion, replace a backup, or guarantee offline use.
storage.lock: Only one tab can write to a disk. If another tab has the disk open, close it before launching again. Do not clear storage or bypass the lock to fix a startup error.
storage.reset: Reset requires explicit confirmation in the disk controls. It stops the old session through a page reload and deletes only the selected overlay before the next boot. Your files, packages, and settings are lost, with no undo. If deletion is blocked, close the other tab.
storage.transferTitle: Full disk export and import are not available
storage.transfer: The shell does not currently support exporting or restoring a complete overlay, exporting RAM, or moving a running session. Do not keep the only copy of important files here.

network.intro: Tailscale is optional and connects only when you choose to. The desktop can start without guest networking; your browser's connection for downloading the runtime and image is separate.

account.title: Use your own Tailscale account
account.detail: Open the network controls on /run and start connecting. Sign in on the official Tailscale website and approve the device in your own tailnet.

exit.title: Set up an external exit node
exit.detail: Guest access to the public internet requires your own configured and approved exit node and a suitable tailnet policy. This can be another computer or a VPS. PocketOSix does not provide a shared exit node.

check.title: Check access inside the guest
check.detail: Use curl or wget if installed. Access depends on your tailnet policy and exit node availability. A Tailscale IP alone does not prove internet access, and ping is not a sufficient check.

network.securityTitle: Keep your network and credentials safe
network.security: Connecting may give the guest access to your private network. Connect only an environment you trust. Never put auth keys, tokens, or passwords in code, URLs, logs, or NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables: those variables are public.

compatibility.title: Supported userspace
compatibility.detail: CheerpX runs supported 32-bit x86 Linux userspace via WebAssembly and syscall compatibility. There is no Linux kernel. This is not Docker, systemd, or a full hardware VM; some syscalls and applications are unsupported, including 64-bit binaries.

dependencies.title: External downloads
dependencies.detail: Compute runs on your device, but the CheerpX runtime and base disk come from external services. Uncached resources need internet access; fully offline use is not guaranteed.

browser.title: Browser requirements
browser.detail: Use a current desktop Chrome or Edge with WebAssembly, SharedArrayBuffer, IndexedDB, and Web Locks. Other browsers and mobile devices are not claimed as verified.

accessibility.title: Guest accessibility
accessibility.detail: The web shell has keyboard-accessible controls. This does not imply full screen reader access to the guest Xorg display.

limits.isolation: Startup requires HTTPS or localhost and cross-origin isolation. If the browser check fails on /run, follow its fix hint. Hosting must preserve COOP / COEP; disabling COEP is not a fix for a CDN error.

license.original: PocketOSix's original code and documentation are MIT-licensed.
license.sdk: The CheerpX SDK and runtime are proprietary, not MIT. Organizational production use requires an appropriate commercial agreement with Leaning Technologies. The PocketOSix license does not permit copying or self-hosting the runtime.
license.packages: Alpine and third-party packages have their own licenses. Reused WebVM code and assets retain their Apache-2.0 notices and attribution.

notFound.title: Page not found.
notFound.detail: This address does not exist. Return to the home page or open the docs for help getting started.

tailscale.title: Waiting for Tailscale sign-in.
tailscale.detail: When Tailscale responds, the original tab will open the sign-in page here. This screen does not connect the network by itself.
tailscale.security: Do not enter passwords or keys here. Sign-in takes place on the official Tailscale website.
tailscale.hint: If nothing opens, check the network status in the original /run tab. Guest access to the public internet also requires an external exit node and a suitable tailnet policy.
